investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC only: curl (plain HTTP GET, descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser/JS execution) against the venue's own official '/fr/agenda/' listing page AND one sampled per-event detail page, to honestly check whether a calendar year is available anywhere on this source (list page, detail page, or a referenced feed/API) before concluding it genuinely is not.

probe_history.reason: A plain curl GET of http://www.lamaroquinerie.fr/fr/agenda/ (note: la-maroquinerie.com is an unrelated leather-goods business, confirmed NOT used) returned 50 static '<li class="event">' cards, each with title, a detail-page URL carrying a stable numeric ID, and a '<h3 class="date">' text — but that date text is ONLY 'DD monthname' (e.g. '30 septembre', ' 1 octobre'), with no year anywhere on any of the 50 cards. A further sampled per-event detail page (https://www.lamaroquinerie.fr/fr/agenda/view/2105/yse/) confirmed the SAME 'DD monthname'-only date text, no JSON-LD, no sitemap/feed reference, and no CMS/theme fingerprint (WordPress, Events Calendar, etc.) anywhere on the site — a bespoke, legacy PHP-templated site ('themes/default/js/...'). This fully and honestly answered the investigation question at Level 1: every other field (title, time, venue, source_record_id, event_url) is cleanly resolvable, but a calendar YEAR is genuinely never published anywhere this investigation could find, on either page tier. No further escalation was pursued, per this policy's 'DEFER/HUMAN_REVIEW does not require exhausting the ladder' — a browser/headless session would not surface a fact this source's own markup never states.

site_classification.platform: A bespoke, legacy PHP-templated site (no WordPress/wp-json, no Events-Calendar, no JSON-LD, no ICS/RSS feed found). Every event is a static, repeated '<li class="event">' card on the '/fr/agenda/' listing page itself. Ticket purchase links point to third-party platforms per-event (Weezevent, Shotgun observed directly on sampled cards) — first-party for acquisition purposes (title/date/venue), but never used as price authority.

title.notes: Each card's own '<h2>' (thumbnail heading), stated directly.

start_date.notes: Every one of the 50 sampled cards' own '<h3 class="date">' states ONLY a day-of-month and a month name (e.g. ' 1 octobre'), never a year. No page heading, section, breadcrumb, meta tag, JSON-LD, or sampled per-event detail page states a year anywhere in this investigation's retained evidence — there is no second retained piece of first-party context to mechanically combine with the day/month (the v1.2 DETERMINISTIC_CONTEXT worked-example table's own 'no month/year context at all' non-example applies directly here; inferring a year from today's date would be AI_INFERENCE and is explicitly prohibited). Left honestly PARTIAL: day+month are DIRECT_SOURCE-known, the year is genuinely unresolved from retained context alone. One sampled card (LOUVE) additionally illustrates why guessing would be actively harmful: its own free-text description states the event was 'reporté au 24 février 2027' (postponed to 24 February 2027) — a completely different year than naive 'current year' rollover would ever produce for a card showing '30 septembre'.

blockers.description: start_date's calendar year is not published anywhere on this source (list page, sampled detail page, or any discoverable feed/JSON-LD) — it can only be recovered by an explicit, human-authorised policy decision (e.g. an operator-approved 'assume the nearest future occurrence of this day/month at true collection time' rule, itself an OPERATOR_DECISION this AI investigation cannot make on its own authority per this policy's anti-guessing rule), or by re-investigating if the source ever adds a year to its own markup. This is a genuine, permanent source limitation, not an escalation-solvable acquisition problem — the LOUVE card's own retained postponement text ('reporté au 24 février 2027' for a card still showing '30 septembre') demonstrates that a naive 'current/next year' assumption would have been actively wrong here.

reasons: Identity PROVEN, acquisition_class STATIC_HTML resolved at Level 1, and title/time/venue_location/source_record_id/event_url are all cleanly PROVEN with basis DIRECT_SOURCE — this is a clean, non-hostile, fully first-party static source.

The sole blocker is start_date.state PARTIAL: no retained page, section, or per-event detail page anywhere states a calendar year, and no second piece of first-party context exists to mechanically combine per v1.2's DETERMINISTIC_CONTEXT rule. Inferring a year from today's date or from 'this is probably the current concert season' would be exactly the AI_INFERENCE this policy prohibits from ever being marked PROVEN.

A real, retained example (LOUVE, 'reporté au 24 février 2027' shown against a card still dated '30 septembre') demonstrates this is not a hypothetical risk: a naive year-rollover assumption would have been concretely wrong for this exact source.

This is a genuine, permanent source-side limitation rather than an access/escalation problem, so HUMAN_REVIEW (not further probing, and not READY_FOR_ACTIVATION) is the honest decision: a human operator may choose to explicitly authorise a documented year-assignment policy (e.g. a real-time 'nearest future occurrence' collector rule, evaluated at actual collection time rather than at investigation time) as an OPERATOR_DECISION, which this investigation itself cannot self-authorise.
No collector code was built for this source in this pass, consistent with HUMAN_REVIEW not requiring READY_FOR_OFFLINE_PROOF/ACTIVATION's offline-proof gate.
